questions.stem: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is acidic when dissolved in water but not when dissolved in a non-polar solvent like methylbenzene. What does this tell us about what makes a solution acidic?

options.text: HCl is only an acid when it is warm
Acids need water to ionise and release H+ ions, which cause acidic properties
Methylbenzene neutralises the acid
HCl changes its chemical formula in different solvents

questions.explanation: Acidic properties are caused by H+ ions (hydrogen ions / protons) in solution. In water, HCl ionises: HCl -> H+ + Cl-. In non-polar solvents, HCl molecules remain intact and do not ionise, so no H+ ions are released and the solution is not acidic. Water is essential for acids to display their characteristic properties.

questions.stem: A student has three unlabelled bottles containing hydrochloric acid (HCl), sulfuric acid (H2SO4), and nitric acid (HNO3). She knows all are at the same concentration. Which property would be the SAME for all three?

options.text: The salts they produce with sodium hydroxide
Their pH value (assuming same concentration of H+)
The volume of gas produced with magnesium
Their chemical formulae

questions.explanation: If all three acids are at the same concentration and are all strong acids (fully ionised), they would produce the same concentration of H+ ions and therefore have the same pH. However, they produce different salts (chlorides, sulfates, nitrates), and H2SO4 is diprotic (2 H+ per molecule) which complicates the comparison. The key concept is that pH depends on H+ concentration.

questions.stem: Citric acid is found in lemons, and ethanoic acid is found in vinegar. Both are safe to consume in food. However, sulfuric acid is extremely dangerous. What is the key difference?

options.text: Citric and ethanoic acids are not really acids
Citric and ethanoic acids are weak acids (partially ionised), while sulfuric acid is a strong acid (fully ionised), giving a much higher H+ concentration
Sulfuric acid contains sulfur, which is poisonous
Food acids are alkaline, not acidic

questions.explanation: Citric acid and ethanoic acid are weak acids - they only partially ionise in water, producing a relatively low concentration of H+ ions. Sulfuric acid is a strong acid that fully ionises, producing a much higher concentration of H+ ions at the same concentration. The higher H+ concentration makes it much more corrosive and dangerous.

questions.stem: Which formula correctly represents sulfuric acid?

options.text: HCl
HNO3
H2SO4
H3PO4

questions.explanation: H2SO4 is sulfuric acid. HCl is hydrochloric acid, HNO3 is nitric acid, and H3PO4 is phosphoric acid. At GCSE, you need to know the three common acids: hydrochloric acid (HCl), sulfuric acid (H2SO4), and nitric acid (HNO3). The number of H atoms tells you how many H+ ions each molecule can release.

questions.stem: Acid rain damages limestone buildings and statues. Limestone is calcium carbonate. What products form when acid rain (containing sulfuric acid) reacts with limestone?

options.text: Calcium sulfate, water, and carbon dioxide
Calcium chloride, water, and carbon dioxide
Calcium nitrate, water, and oxygen
Calcium oxide and sulfur dioxide

questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate -> salt + water + carbon dioxide. With sulfuric acid: H2SO4 + CaCO3 -> CaSO4 + H2O + CO2. Sulfuric acid produces sulfate salts, hydrochloric acid produces chloride salts, and nitric acid produces nitrate salts. The fizzing observed when acid rain attacks limestone is carbon dioxide gas being released.
